raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
Allow DSA index-K elision under HiSparse decode to reclaim GPU memory and raise batch size.

## Motivation

DeepSeek-DSA's IndexShare lets most layers share a single top-k selection: these
"shared" layers reuse a preceding producer layer's top-k and never read or write
their own index-K. GLM-5.2 has 78 layers, of which only 21 are producers and 57
are shared.

The device pool already allocates 0 index-K pages for the shared layers via
`skip_topk_layers`, but `_should_elide_dsa_index_k()` still refused elision under
HiSparse on a PD decode engine, so the 57 shared layers held device buffers for
nothing. This commit opens elision on that path and returns the memory to the KV
pool.

## Modifications

- `kv_cache_configurator.py`: allow `_should_elide_dsa_index_k` to elide on a
  HiSparse PD decode engine. The prefill peer runs the indexer on every layer and
  writes its own index-K, so only the decode engine can drop these rows; a single
  engine (`disaggregation_mode == "null"`) and prefill still keep the full set.
- `pool_configurator.py`: drop the `or enable_hisparse` short-circuit so the
  sizing path and the allocation path read the same predicate. Previously sizing
  priced all 78 layers while allocation already saved 21, so
  `max_total_num_tokens` did not reflect the reclaimed memory.
- Under HiSparse, index-K resides on device at logical capacity ×
  `host_to_device_ratio`, so the saving is multiplied by the same factor.
- Kill switch: `SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXK_ELISION=1`.

No PD transfer-protocol change is needed: a shared layer's buffer is 0 bytes, so
`_registerable_regions()` skips the zero-length region (Mooncake rejects a zero
length memory region) and the sender's `is_elided_entry` drops the matching
transfer entry. The hierarchical-cache host (L2) index-K pool is likewise packed:
one host layer per index-K-owning device layer.

## Accuracy Tests

GLM-5.2 NVFP4, 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP8/PP1, PD disaggregation with HiSparse
on the decode engine, 5-shot GSM8K, temperature=0, `--parallel 16`. Each arm
fully restarts PD and changes only the kill switch; after restart the decode-side
`max_total_num_tokens` is 206144 (off) / 402752 (on), confirming the two arms are
different pools.

| num-questions | elision | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 200  | off | 0.960 | 0.000 |
| 200  | on  | 0.940 | 0.000 |
| 1000 | off | 0.949 | 0.000 |
| 1000 | on  | 0.946 | 0.000 |

At n=1000 the two arms differ by 0.3pp (3/1000 questions), within the 1%–5%
variance CONTRIBUTING documents for this script; the n=200 gap of 2.0pp (4
questions) is too small a sample to be meaningful. This matches the structural
argument: shared layers never read their own index-K (`dsa_layer_skips_topk()`
plus the existing `skip_topk_layers` path), so not allocating it is a no-op and
does not change model outputs.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

GLM-5.2 NVFP4, 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP8/PP1, PD disaggregation with HiSparse
on the decode engine, `host_to_device_ratio=10`, `device_buffer_size=4096`,
shared-index prefetch off, decode `--mem-fraction-static 0.90` / prefill `0.80`,
128K input, O=2000, full prefix hit on the prefill side. Batch size is the
largest concurrency the decode pool admits without retraction. Latencies are
sampled after the client's initial burst has drained.

| Arm | Device pool tokens | Batch size | Output tput | Per-GPU | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| elision off | 206,144 | 15 | 325.7 tok/s | 40.7 tok/s | 45.5 ms |
| elision on  | 402,752 | 30 | 436.5 tok/s | 54.6 tok/s | 67.1 ms |

The device pool grows 1.954×, matching the per-token cost ratio 154,128/78,888
(78 × 656 B latent KV plus 132 B per indexer layer × ratio). Doubling concurrency
(batch 15 → 30) trades latency for throughput: aggregate throughput +34.0%
(325.7 → 436.5 tok/s) and per-GPU +34.2% (40.7 → 54.6 tok/s), at the cost of TPOT
+47.5% (45.5 → 67.1 ms). Latency-sensitive deployments can fall back to the
smaller pool via the kill switch. Both arms show `err=0`, `#queue-req: 0`,
`#retracted-req: 0`.

## Checklist

- [x] pre-commit formatting
- [x] Docs: add `docs/docs/advanced_features/dsa_index_k_elision.mdx`, register it
      in `docs.json` navigation, and link to it from the shared-index prefetch
      section of `hisparse_guide.mdx`
- [x] Unit tests:
      - `test_dsa_index_k_elision_gate.py` (new, CPU): the predicate decision
        table, covering draft, kill switch, external linker, NPU PD / hierarchical,
        every non-HiSparse role, and HiSparse-decode-only — 7 branches
      - `test_hisparse_pool_configurator.py`: HiSparse decode prices only producer
        layers (2888 B); a single engine / prefill prices every layer (3680 B)
      - `test_dsa_pool_host_unit.py`: 0-row buffers, the `item_len`/`data_len`
        zeroing the PD wire layer trims on, the packed host indexer pool, and the
        HiSparse-pool elision with its ratio scaling

@@ -0,0 +1,64 @@
+---
+title: "DSA Index-K Elision for Shared-Index Layers"
+metatags:
+    description: "Reclaim the index-K cache of DSA layers that reuse another layer's top-k selection, raising decode capacity for HiSparse, HiCache, and single-engine serving."
+---
+
+Some DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) models share one top-k selection across several layers. GLM-5.2 is an example: its IndexShare pattern runs the indexer on an anchor layer and lets the following "skip" layers reuse the anchor's top-k (`index_topk_freq` / `index_topk_pattern`). A skip layer builds no indexer, so its index-K cache is never written or read. SGLang gives those layers a zero-row index-K buffer and spends the reclaimed memory on more KV tokens, which raises the maximum decode batch size.
+
+The optimization is on by default. It does not change model outputs.
+
+## When elision applies
+
+Elision applies to the target model's KV pool only. The MTP / NextN draft pool always keeps a full indexer.
+
+| Deployment | Elided? |
+|---|---|
+| Single engine, no HiSparse | Yes |
+| PD prefill or decode, no HiSparse | Yes |
+| Hierarchical cache (`--enable-hierarchical-cache`), no HiSparse | Yes |
+| PD decode with HiSparse (`--enable-hisparse`) | Yes |
+| Single engine or PD prefill with HiSparse | No |
+| MTP / NextN draft pool | No |
+| `--enable-unified-cache-external-linker` | No |
+| Ascend NPU with PD, or Ascend NPU with hierarchical cache | No |
+
+HiSparse is the one case that depends on the PD role. A HiSparse prefill peer still runs the indexer on every layer and writes its own index-K, so only the decode engine can drop the rows.
+
+Elision needs no change to the PD transfer protocol. A skip layer's buffer is zero bytes, so the RDMA path never registers a memory region for it and the sender drops the matching transfer entry. The hierarchical-cache host (L2) index-K pool is likewise packed: it allocates one host layer per indexer-owning device layer and maps device layer ids onto those compact slots.
+
+## Memory impact
+
+The saving is proportional to the fraction of skip layers. For GLM-5.2 (78 layers, 21 with an indexer, FP8 KV cache) the per-token cost of the device KV pool is `78 × 656 B` of latent KV plus `132 B` per indexer-owning layer:
+
+| Pool | Elision off | Elision on | Change |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Plain DSA or HiCache decode | 51,168 + 78 × 132 = 61,464 B | 51,168 + 21 × 132 = 53,940 B | +14% tokens |
+| HiSparse decode, `host_to_device_ratio=10` | 51,168 + 78 × 132 × 10 = 154,128 B | 51,168 + 21 × 132 × 10 = 78,888 B | +95% tokens |
+
+HiSparse stores index-K at logical (host) capacity on the device, so its saving is multiplied by `host_to_device_ratio`. The host pool holds `max_total_num_tokens × host_to_device_ratio` tokens, so decode concurrency is bounded by that capacity divided by each request's `input_len + output_len`, and it grows by the same factor as the pool.
+
+<Note>
+HiSparse keeps the full KV of every request in host memory, so doubling the device pool also doubles the host memory requirement. Size `host_to_device_ratio` against your host RAM; see the [HiSparse guide](./hisparse_guide).
+</Note>
+
+## Disabling elision
+
+Set the kill-switch on the engine whose pool you want to keep full, typically the decode instance:
+
+```bash
+SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXK_ELISION=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server ...
+```
+
+Use it for A/B comparisons or to roll back. The prefill instance needs no change in either case.
+
+## Measured results
+
+GLM-5.2 NVFP4 on 8× RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), TP8 / PP1, PD disaggregation with HiSparse on the decode engine, `host_to_device_ratio=10`, `device_buffer_size=4096`, shared-index prefetch off, decode `--mem-fraction-static 0.90`, prefill `0.80`, 128K input, 2,000 output tokens, full prefix hit on the prefill engine. Batch size is the largest offered concurrency the decode pool admits without retraction. Latencies are sampled after the client's initial burst has drained, so they reflect steady state. These numbers come from a `--pp-size 1` deployment; elision itself does not depend on the pipeline-parallel degree.
+
+| Arm | Device pool tokens | Batch size | Output throughput | Per-GPU throughput | TPOT |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| Elision off | 206,144 | 15 | 325.7 tok/s | 40.7 tok/s | 45.5 ms |
+| Elision on | 402,752 | 30 | 436.5 tok/s | 54.6 tok/s | 67.1 ms |
+
+The pool grows by 1.954×, which matches the per-token cost ratio 154,128 / 78,888 above. Serving twice the concurrent requests on the same GPUs trades per-request latency for aggregate throughput: output throughput rises 34% while TPOT rises 48% (45.5 → 67.1 ms). Pick the arm that matches your latency budget; the kill-switch above restores the smaller pool.

+"""CPU decision table for `_should_elide_dsa_index_k`.
+
+Skip-topk DSA layers build no Indexer, so the forward never writes their
+index-K and the pool can give them a 0-row buffer. This gate decides when that
+is safe; the sizing path (`pool_configurator`) and the allocation path
+(`KVCacheConfigurator`) must both read the same answer, so pin it here.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest import mock
+
+from sglang.srt.mem_cache import kv_cache_configurator as kvcc
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_cpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_cpu_ci(est_time=5, stage="base-a", runner_config="cpu")
+
+
+class TestDSAIndexKElisionGate(CustomTestCase):
+    def _elide(
+        self,
+        *,
+        is_draft=False,
+        disabled=False,
+        disagg="null",
+        hisparse=False,
+        hierarchical=False,
+        external_linker=False,
+        is_npu=False,
+    ):
+        memory = SimpleNamespace(
+            enable_hisparse=hisparse,
+            enable_hierarchical_cache=hierarchical,
+            enable_unified_cache_external_linker=external_linker,
+        )
+        fake_envs = SimpleNamespace(
+            SGLANG_DISABLE_DSA_INDEXK_ELISION=SimpleNamespace(get=lambda: disabled),
+        )
+        with (
+            mock.patch.object(kvcc, "get_memory", lambda: memory),
+            mock.patch.object(
+                kvcc,
+                "get_disagg",
+                lambda: SimpleNamespace(disaggregation_mode=disagg),
+            ),
+            mock.patch.object(kvcc, "envs", fake_envs),
+            mock.patch.object(kvcc, "_is_npu", is_npu),
+        ):
+            return kvcc._should_elide_dsa_index_k(is_draft_worker=is_draft)
+
+    def test_draft_worker_never_elides(self):
+        # The MTP/NextN draft pool keeps its own indexer on every layer.
+        self.assertFalse(self._elide(is_draft=True))
+
+    def test_kill_switch_disables(self):
+        self.assertFalse(self._elide(disabled=True))
+        self.assertFalse(self._elide(disabled=True, disagg="decode", hisparse=True))
+
+    def test_external_linker_never_elides(self):
+        # The linker hands rows to an out-of-tree owner that assumes a dense
+        # per-layer layout.
+        self.assertFalse(self._elide(external_linker=True))
+
+    def test_npu_pd_never_elides(self):
+        # Ascend PD slices the KV list positionally (index-K rides in it rather
+        # than in StateType.DSA), so a compact layout would mis-slice.
+        for disagg in ("prefill", "decode"):
+            with self.subTest(disagg=disagg):
+                self.assertFalse(self._elide(is_npu=True, disagg=disagg))
+        self.assertTrue(self._elide(is_npu=True, disagg="null"))
+
+    def test_npu_hierarchical_never_elides(self):

+class TestDSAIndexKElision(CustomTestCase):
+    """Skip-topk layers get a 0-row index-K buffer, and the host (L2) indexer
+    pool packs only the layers that actually own index keys."""
+
+    def setUp(self):
+        if not torch.cuda.is_available():
+            self.skipTest("CUDA is required for DSA pool allocation tests.")
+        if is_npu() or is_xpu() or not (is_cuda() or is_hip()):
+            self.skipTest("DSA pool allocation tests only support CUDA/ROCm.")
+        cm = get_parallel().override(attn_dcp_size=1)
+        cm.__enter__()
+        self.addCleanup(cm.__exit__, None, None, None)
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _build_pool(page_size: int, skip_topk_layers):
+        return DSATokenToKVPool(
+            size=page_size * 4,
+            page_size=page_size,
+            kv_lora_rank=128,
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            qk_rope_head_dim=32,
+            layer_num=len(skip_topk_layers),
+            device="cuda",
+            enable_memory_saver=False,
+            kv_cache_dim=576,
+            index_head_dim=128,
+            skip_topk_layers=skip_topk_layers,
+        )
+
+    def test_skip_topk_layers_get_zero_row_buffers(self):
+        page_size = 1 if is_hip() else 64
+        # Layer 1 reuses layer 0's top-k, so it never writes index-K.
+        pool = self._build_pool(page_size, [False, True, False])
+
+        buffers = pool.index_k_with_scale_buffer
+        self.assertEqual(buffers[1].shape[0], 0)
+        self.assertGreater(buffers[0].shape[0], 0)
+        self.assertGreater(buffers[2].shape[0], 0)
+
+        # The PD wire layer trims on these: a 0-byte region is never registered
+        # (Mooncake rejects it) and `is_elided_entry` drops the transfer pair.
+        _, data_lens, item_lens = pool.get_state_buf_infos()
+        self.assertEqual(data_lens[1], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(item_lens[1], 0)
+        self.assertGreater(item_lens[0], 0)
+        self.assertGreater(item_lens[2], 0)
+
+    def test_all_layers_owned_when_nothing_is_skipped(self):
+        page_size = 1 if is_hip() else 64
+        pool = self._build_pool(page_size, [False, False])
+
+        self.assertTrue(all(buf.shape[0] > 0 for buf in pool.index_k_with_scale_buffer))
+        _, data_lens, item_lens = pool.get_state_buf_infos()
+        self.assertTrue(all(length > 0 for length in data_lens))
+        self.assertTrue(all(length > 0 for length in item_lens))
+
+    def test_host_indexer_pool_packs_only_owning_layers(self):
+        page_size = 1 if is_hip() else 64
+        skip_topk_layers = [False, True, False, True]
+        pool = self._build_pool(page_size, skip_topk_layers)
+
+        decl = make_dsa_indexer_pool_decl(pool)
+        self.assertEqual(decl.owned_device_layers, (0, 2))
+
+        original_alloc = ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS["cuda"]
+        ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS["cuda"] = alloc_with_pin_memory
+        try:
+            mla_host = _build_mla_host(pool, page_size, pin_memory=True)
+            indexer_host = DSAIndexerPoolHost(
+                decl=decl,
+                anchor_host=mla_host,
+                pin_memory=True,
+                device="cpu",
+                allocator_type="default",
+            )
+        finally:
+            ALLOC_MEMORY_FUNCS["cuda"] = original_alloc
+
+        # Host storage is compacted: 2 owning layers out of 4 device layers,
+        # addressed by compact slot rather than by device layer id.
+        self.assertEqual(indexer_host.target_layer_num, 2)
+        self.assertEqual(indexer_host._host_layer_index(0), 0)
+        self.assertEqual(indexer_host._host_layer_index(2), 1)
+        self.assertEqual(sorted(indexer_host._device_to_host_layer), [0, 2])
+
+    def test_pool_declares_no_indexer_host_when_every_layer_skips(self):
+        page_size = 1 if is_hip() else 64
+        pool = self._build_pool(page_size, [True, True])
+
+        # No layer owns index keys, so there is nothing to mirror to the host.
+        names = [decl.pool_name for decl in pool.host_pool_decls()]
+        self.assertNotIn(PoolName.INDEXER, names)
+
+    def test_hisparse_pool_elides_and_scales_the_saving_by_the_ratio(self):
+        # HiSparse sizes index-K at logical (host) capacity on the device via
+        # `index_buf_size = size * host_to_device_ratio`, so eliding a skip layer
+        # saves ratio times as much as on a plain DSA pool. The elide decision
+        # still arrives as the same `skip_topk_layers` kwarg.
+        page_size = 1 if is_hip() else 64
+        ratio = 2
+
+        def build(skip_topk_layers):
+            return HiSparseDSATokenToKVPool(
+                size=page_size * 4,
+                page_size=page_size,
+                kv_lora_rank=128,
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+                qk_rope_head_dim=32,
+                layer_num=len(skip_topk_layers),
+                device="cuda",
+                index_head_dim=128,
+                enable_memory_saver=False,
+                kv_cache_dim=576,
+                skip_topk_layers=skip_topk_layers,
+                host_to_device_ratio=ratio,
+            )
+
+        elided = build([False, True, False, True])
+        self.assertEqual(elided.index_k_with_scale_buffer[1].shape[0], 0)
+        self.assertEqual(elided.index_k_with_scale_buffer[3].shape[0], 0)
+        _, data_lens, item_lens = elided.get_state_buf_infos()
+        self.assertEqual([data_lens[1], data_lens[3]], [0, 0])
+        self.assertEqual([item_lens[1], item_lens[3]], [0, 0])
+
+        full = build([False, False, False, False])
+        elided_bytes = sum(b.nbytes for b in elided.index_k_with_scale_buffer)
+        full_bytes = sum(b.nbytes for b in full.index_k_with_scale_buffer)
+        # 2 of 4 layers own index-K.
+        self.assertEqual(elided_bytes * 2, full_bytes)
+        # Each owning layer still covers the full logical host capacity.
+        rows_per_owning_layer = elided.index_k_with_scale_buffer[0].shape[0]
+        self.assertEqual(
+            rows_per_owning_layer, full.index_k_with_scale_buffer[0].shape[0]
+        )
+        self.assertGreater(rows_per_owning_layer, 0)
+

+    def test_hisparse_decode_prices_only_indexer_owning_layers(self):
+        # One anchor layer plus three shared-topk layers. On a HiSparse decode
+        # engine the shared layers own no index-K, so the cell must price one
+        # indexer layer, not four. The sizing path and the allocation path read
+        # the same `_should_elide_dsa_index_k`; if sizing priced all four,
+        # max_total_num_tokens would hide the memory the pool never allocates.
+        #
+        # fp8 cell = 656 B/layer latent + 132 B/token/indexer-layer * ratio:
+        #   decode  (1 priced layer)  = 4 * 656 + 132 * 1 * 2 = 2888
+        #   prefill (4 priced layers) = 4 * 656 + 132 * 4 * 2 = 3680
+        kwargs = dict(
+            enable_hisparse=True,
+            host_to_device_ratio=2,
+            num_layers=4,
+            index_topk_pattern=["A", "S", "S", "S"],
+        )

+        )
+        prefill_cell = self._compute_cell_size(
+            torch.float8_e4m3fn, disaggregation_mode="prefill", **kwargs
+        )

+        self.assertEqual(prefill_cell, 3680)
